## 2.1 Cores and threads

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A **core** is a small processor inside the CPU. It runs one **thread** at a time.
- Big cores are fast; small cores save battery.
- The game logic runs on one main thread, so it always uses one core.
- GHz tells the speed of **one** core. Cores do not add up.
- **Do it:** Open Task Manager → Performance → CPU. How many logical processors do you see?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/cpu-cores.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Splitting one frame

One frame needs 10 ms on the main thread and 6 ms of work that the cores share.
**How long is the frame with 1, 2 and 6 cores?**

::: {.reveal}
1. 1 core: 10 + 6 = **16 ms**.
2. 2 cores share the 6 ms: 10 + 3 = **13 ms**.
3. 6 cores share the 6 ms: 10 + 1 = **11 ms**.
4. The frame is faster, but not 6 times faster.
:::

## Try it 1 · Cores and threads

A frame needs 8 ms on the main thread and 4 ms of work that the cores share equally.

a) How long is the frame with four cores?
b) Which core is best for music in the background, with little battery?
c) A phone has 8 cores at 3 GHz. How fast is the core of the main thread?

::: {.answer}
a) 9 ms (8 + 1)
b) an efficiency core
c) 3 GHz
:::

## 2.2 The memory hierarchy

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Memory has levels: cache, then RAM, then storage.
- The levels near the core are small and fast.
- The levels far from the core are big, slow and cheap.
- A read from the cache takes 1 ns; a read from RAM takes 100 ns.
- **Do it:** In Data Trip, fetch one value from each level. Which level is the fastest?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/memory-hierarchy.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 2 · The memory hierarchy

A read from the cache takes 1 ns. A read from RAM takes 100 ns.

a) A read takes about 100 ns. Which level of the hierarchy is it?
b) The player's position is read 50 times in one frame. Where does the core find it after the first read?
c) Where is the best score kept when the phone is off?

::: {.answer}
a) RAM
b) in the cache
c) in storage
:::

## 2.3 Why the game shows a loading screen

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Installing copies the app package into storage.
- Launching creates a process and loads code and assets into RAM.
- The speed of storage sets the loading time.
- **Do it:** In Task Manager → Processes, sort by Memory. Which app uses the most?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](../week-01/images/launch.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Cheap phone, slow loading

A level needs 1500 MB of assets. Phone A reads 1500 MB per second, and phone B reads 150 MB per second.
**How long does the level load on each phone?**

::: {.reveal}
1. Phone A needs 1500 ÷ 1500 = **1 second**.
2. Phone B needs 1500 ÷ 150 = **10 seconds**.
3. The game is the same; only the **speed of storage** is different.
:::

## Try it 3 · Install, launch, load

a) What does a player fill when installing a game?
b) How long do 900 MB of assets load at 300 MB per second?
c) A game update is 2 GB. How many MB is that?

::: {.answer}
a) storage
b) 3 seconds
c) 2048 MB (2 × 1024)
:::

## 2.4 Storage

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A hard disk has spinning disks and a moving arm. It is cheap but slow.
- An SSD and a phone use flash chips with no moving parts.
- A game in storage has three parts: the app, the user data and the cache.
- **Do it:** Open a game's storage screen on your phone. How big is each part?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/storage.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 4 · Storage

a) A player presses Clear cache. What do they lose?
b) A player wants free space but wants to keep the pets. Which button must they not press?
c) A "1 TB" SSD shows 931 GB in Windows. Is space missing?

::: {.answer}
a) nothing important (only temporary files)
b) Clear storage
c) No. The maker counts in 1000, Windows in 1024.
:::

## Try it · Answer the players (harder)

The facts: the new island of Pocket Pets 2.0 has 900 MB. A cheap phone reads 180 MB per second.

a) The island needs 1.6 GB, and a phone has 1.2 GB free. How much more space is needed?
b) A player pressed Clear storage, and the pets are gone. Which part was deleted?
c) How long does the island take to load on the cheap phone?

::: {.answer}
a) 0.4 GB
b) the user data
c) 5 seconds (900 ÷ 180)
:::

## Summary

- A core runs one thread, so 8 cores do not make a game 8 times faster.
- Memory has levels: cache, RAM and storage, from fast to slow.
- The cache keeps the data that the game uses again and again.
- Launching loads the game into RAM, and the speed of storage sets the loading time.
- Storage holds the app, the user data and the cache.
